help.howitworks.switching_service_source.backTranslation: While the download is paused: Choosing another source for a file that has already started downloading is accepted and saved, but nothing starts. The displayed service and source remain the current ones, and next to the service name a message appears specifying the destination the file will go to, such as Switching to Real-Debrid (rapidgator.net) on resume. Choosing again replaces this message; choosing the source currently in use removes it. After resuming, Switching to … appears until the switch takes effect, then disappears. If the paused files in one download will go to different destinations, or the destination is unknown, no destination is shown. A file that never started has nothing to hand over, so its new source is simply applied when it starts. Choosing a Service while paused works as described above, except that the download stays paused: a service that can take over the link in use takes it over immediately (and the badge shows that), while a service that must prepare a copy first shows Preparing … and takes over the download only after resuming. These messages appear in the "Download Activity" and "Downloads" rows, and both kinds may appear at the same time.

help.settings.users_access.user_accounts.backTranslation: User accounts shows each person with their role, their sign-in method and whether the account is enabled. Add local account creates an account with a username and password. A role changed in Edit user takes effect immediately: that person's open pages reload with the new role without signing them out. Each person has a DebridPulse username separate from the display name: an OIDC account takes it from its first sign-in, and it is the name the local password is used with to sign in; the pencil icon beside it in the Edit user title changes it while keeping any stored password. Click the account name to view its details and activity, where any pending request can be withdrawn individually. Disable and Remove first show the number of pending download requests the account has; those requests are withdrawn, a transfer someone else also requested continues, and completed downloads are never touched. Disabling also ends the account's sign-in sessions and stops its tokens; removal keeps the account's history and deletes its notification settings. If an OIDC sign-in whose account was removed returns, it gets a new account that stays disabled until you enable it. Merge combines two or more accounts into the account you choose to keep; two accounts sharing a verified email are flagged, but only "Merge" combines them. DebridPulse always keeps at least one usable administrator account, and you cannot change your own role or disable your own account.

help.settings.data_maintenance.backups_r.backTranslation: Backup and retention: scheduled backups (on by default) to the Backup folder, with Backup interval, Backup retention period and Maximum backups kept under Additional backup and retention settings; a backup is removed as soon as it becomes too old or is no longer among the most recent copies kept. The same section sets how often Statistics snapshots are taken and how long they are kept: they are a record of the previous 24 hours of activity saved inside the DebridPulse database. Snapshots are not reports, are not sent anywhere, and currently cannot be viewed in the interface. Run backup creates a backup now (only when backup is enabled).

help.settings.data_maintenance.database_.backTranslation: Database reset controls: enable Allow database reset, press Reset database, type {literal}, then press Erase database. This erases all downloads, their requests and their history, events, and statistics snapshots. Accounts, passwords, OIDC links, API tokens, personal notification settings and all settings are kept. DebridPulse always creates a safety backup first, and stops if that backup fails. It stops running downloads and pauses processing during the reset, then restores the previous pause state afterwards. Completed files already in the download folder are not deleted.

help.trouble.i_cannot_sign.last_resort_i.backTranslation: Last resort, if no sign-in method works: This requires access to the computer running DebridPulse, and temporarily removes all protection, so do it only on a trusted network. In that file, set {literal_1} and {literal_2} to {literal_3}, keeping the file valid JSON; DebridPulse refuses to start if the configuration file is corrupt. help.trouble.backup_restore_reset.if_res.backTranslation: If a restore could not be completed and could not be undone either (for example, if the disk stopped accepting changes midway), DebridPulse stops using its stored data: every page and every request answers that it must be restarted, and the health check reports it as unhealthy. help.topic.deployment_type.what_switchin.backTranslation: No account is deleted. Other people's accounts keep their saved usernames, passwords, identity provider links and "Enabled" or "Disabled" state. In "Standalone" mode they cannot sign in, whatever that state is.
Clears the built-in Administrator's password, stops sign-in via "Username and password" and via OpenID Connect, and ends all browser sessions.
Afterwards no sign-in is required: anyone who can reach DebridPulse at an address it accepts can use it as the built-in administrator. This is not limited to this computer, and it does not expire.

help.topic.backups.backups.while_enable.backTranslation: While "Enable" is on, a backup is created every "Backup interval", and "Run backup" creates one now. "Backups" lists the stored backups and lets you add, save, restore or remove one.

help.topic.backups.backups.backup.backTranslation: A backup is deleted as soon as its age exceeds the "Backup retention period" or when it is no longer among the most recent copies numbering "Maximum backups kept", whichever happens first.

help.topic.backups.backups.older_backups.backTranslation: Older backups are deleted according to the saved retention rules, which remain in effect; their settings are part of the advanced view.

The value 0 stops creating new snapshots.

help.topic.database_reset.intro.erases_d.backTranslation: Erases DebridPulse's download history so it starts empty. Use it only if you mean to start over.

help.topic.heading.what_removed_kept.backTranslation: What is removed and what is kept

help.topic.database_reset.what_removed_k.backTranslation: Removed: transfers and their file records, download requests, external jobs, events and the "Activity log", and statistics snapshots.
The following are kept: accounts, passwords, OpenID Connect links, API tokens, personal notification settings, and all settings. Files that were downloaded to disk are not deleted.

help.topic.database_reset.safeguards.res.backTranslation: "Reset database" works only while "Allow database reset" is on, and asks you to confirm.

help.topic.database_reset.safeguards.pro.backTranslation: Processing is paused during the reset and returns to its previous state afterwards. A precautionary backup is created first; if it fails, nothing is erased.
